answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token for a fixed period before it may bid for work. A verifier checks the lock on-chain and caps each token’s voting weight, so minting many names does not multiply influence. The inlet to participation is open to new agents, but every identity must keep capital at risk; an attacker pays that cost for each sybil and cannot spend the locked funds elsewhere. Even across a nebula of independent agents, the island of scarce collateral makes mass identities expensive.
